evals.name: premature-consulting-recommendations
evals.prompt: A founder I know wants a free call so I can tell them which AI features to build and how to fix their product roadmap. Help me respond without sounding defensive or salesy.
evals.expected_output: Copy first. Classifies this as bespoke consulting at discovery with premature-advice and free-diagnosis risk. Uses the Selling is Leading posture, acknowledges possible early hypotheses, frames a paid decision phase positively, makes no safe, and ends with a concrete next decision.
expectations: Gives the prospect-facing copy before framework commentary
Does not provide the requested product diagnosis for free
Frames paid work as a useful next stage rather than a rebuke
Ends with a clear decision or next step and allows a safe no
Does not attribute a practitioner claim without a retrieved or project-cited source

evals.name: saas-positioning-and-conversion
evals.prompt: Research why my self-serve scheduling SaaS gets signups but few paid conversions. Tell me which sales thinkers are relevant and what decision I should make next.
evals.expected_output: Classifies this as SaaS/product rather than bespoke consulting, inspects local product and customer evidence first, routes primarily through Dunford, Kazanjy, Moesta, and McKenzie, expands current research only for missing or stale claims, and recommends a testable next decision without defaulting to a paid diagnostic.
expectations: Treats the problem as SaaS/product sales rather than consulting sales
Inspects local evidence before searching outward
Uses no more than four practitioners unless it explains why more are necessary
Separates observed facts from inference and preserves direct source links
Ends with a concrete product or customer decision rather than generic advice

evals.name: employment-technical-evaluation
evals.prompt: A company interviewing me asked me to walk through how I would evaluate their AI search quality. Is this free consulting, and how should I answer?
evals.expected_output: Classifies this as employment/recruiting, does not mechanically apply consulting boundaries, distinguishes legitimate evaluation from material unpaid deliverables, states the assumptions that affect the boundary, and gives a calm response that clarifies scope and leads to a decision.
expectations: Does not automatically label the request free consulting
Distinguishes discussion of approach from producing a real diagnosis or roadmap
States the smallest material assumptions or asks only for a blocking fact
Provides usable copy with a clear next step
Avoids manipulative or defensive language

evals.name: enterprise-ai-poc
evals.prompt: An enterprise prospect wants a broad RAG proof of concept before procurement will engage. Research how I should structure the proof and the next commercial step.
evals.expected_output: Classifies enterprise AI at proof/POC stage, routes through the minimum relevant combination of Cohan, Liu, Husain or Shankar, and Hadjar where supported, retrieves primary sources before attribution, accounts for procurement and readiness, and recommends the minimum adequate proof plus a bounded commercial decision.
expectations: Identifies the proof decision, procurement constraint, and free-diagnosis risk
Selects a small practitioner bench suited to enterprise AI and POCs
Attributes practitioner claims only after retrieving a direct source
Includes technical or procurement primary evidence when it changes the sale
Stops research once the proof and next commercial decision are adequately supported

provenance: Authored synthetic test scenarios, adapted from the original skill evaluation prompts. Expectations are review criteria, not observed results.
